Dedekind domain.  In the proof of necessity, a key new ingredient is
Artin's approximation theorem; it implies that the topological rings
given by pro-representability can be algebraized.  The resulting schemes
are then glued together via an \'etale equivalence relation.

By checking that the five conditions hold, Artin \cite[Thm.~7.3, p.~67]{Ar67}
proved the following theorem.
 \begin{sbsthm}\label{th:algsp}
  Let $f\:X\to S$ be a flat, proper, and finitely presented map of
algebraic spaces.  Assume forming $f_*\mc O_{\!X}$ commutes with changing
$S$ (or $f$ is ``cohomologically flat in dimension zero'').  Then
$\IPic_{X/S}$ exists as an algebraic space, which is locally of finite
presentation over $S$.
 \end{sbsthm}
 \noindent Since $f$ is finitely presented, the statement can be reduced
to the case where $S$ is locally of finite type over a field or over an
excellent Dedekind domain.  Artin's proof of Theorem~\ref{th:algsp} is
direct: it involves no reduction whatsoever to Theorem~\ref{th:main}.

On the other hand, it is not known, in general, whether
Theorem~\ref{th:algsp} implies Theorem~\ref{th:main}, which asserts
$\IPic_{X/S}$ is a scheme.  However, more is known over a {\it field}.
Indeed, given an algebraic space that is locally of finite type over a
field, Artin \cite[Lem.~4.2, p.~43]{Ar67} proved this: if the space is a
sheaf of groups, then it is a group scheme.  Thus Theorem~\ref{th:algsp}
implies the heart of Corollary ~\ref{cor:algsch}.

Thus, in Theorem~\ref{th:algsp}, the fibers over $S$ of the algebraic
space $\IPic_{X/S}$ are schemes; they are the Picard schemes of the
fibers $X_s$, though the $X_s$ need not be schemes.  In particular, if
$S$ and $X$ are schemes\emdash so the $X_s$ are too\emdash then the
$\IPic_{X_s/k_s}$ are schemes.  Furthermore, then they form a family;
its total space $\IPic_{X/S}$ is an algebraic space, but not necessarily
a scheme.
 \end{rmk}

\section{The connected component of the identity}\label{sc:Pic0}
 Having treated the existence of the Picard scheme $\IPic_{X/S}$, we now
turn to its structure.  In this section, we study the union
$\IPicz_{X/S}$ of the connected components of the identity element,
$\IPicz_{X_s/k_s}$, for $s\in S$.  We establish a number of basic
properties, especially when $S$ is the spectrum of a field.

It is remarkable how much we can prove about $\IPicz_{X/S}$ formally, or
nearly so, from general principles.  Notably, we can do without the
finiteness theorems proved in the next section.  In order to emphasize
the formal nature and corresponding generality of the arguments,
most of the results are stated with the general hypothesis that
$\IPic_{X/S}$ exists instead of with specific hypotheses that imply it
exists.

\begin{lem}\label{lem:agps}
 Let $k$ be a field, and $G$ a group scheme locally of finite
type.  Let $G^0$ denote the connected component of the identity element $e$.

\tu{(1)} Then $G$ is separated.

\tu{(2)} Then $G$ is smooth if it has a geometrically
reduced open subscheme.

 \tu{(3)} Then $G^0$ is an open and closed group subscheme of finite
type; it is geometrically irreducible; and forming it commutes with
extending $k$.
 \end{lem}
 \begin{proof}
 Since $e$ is a $k$-point, it is closed.  Define a map $\alpha\:G\x G\to

$Z\to Q$ such that $R=Z\x_QZ$.  (In other words, a flat and proper
equivalence relation on a quasi-projective scheme is effective.)  In
fact, $R$ defines a map from $Z$ to the Hilbert scheme $\IHilb_{Z/S}$, and
its graph lies in the universal scheme as a closed subscheme, which
descends to $Q\subset \IHilb_{Z/S}$; for more details, see \cite[Thm.~(2.9),
p.~70]{AK80}.

Since $Z\to Q$ is flat, it is smooth if (and only if) its fibers are
smooth.  But these fibers are, up to extension of the ground field, the
same as those of $R\to Z$.  And $R\to Z$ is smooth by hypothesis.  Thus
$Z\to Q$ is smooth.

It remains to see that $Q$ represents $P$.  First, observe that $Z\to Q$
is (represents) a surjection of \'etale sheaves.  Indeed, given an
element of $Q(T)$, set $A:=Z\x_QT$.  Then $A\to T$ is smooth.  So there
exist an \'etale covering $T'\to T$ and a $T$-map $T'\to A$ by
\cite[17.16.3 (ii)]{EGAIV4}.  Then $T'\to A\to Z$ is an element of
$Z(T')$, which maps to the element of $Q(T')$ induced by the given
element of $Q(T)$.

Since $Z\to Q$ is a surjection of \'etale sheaves, $Q$ is, in the
category of \'etale sheaves, the coequalizer of the pair of maps
$R\rightrightarrows Z$ by Exercise~\ref{ex:epi} below, which is an
elementary exercise in general Grothendieck topology.  By the same
exercise, $P$ too is the coequalizer of this pair of maps.  But, in any
category, the coequalizer is unique up to unique isomorphism.  Thus $Q$
represents $P$.
 \end{proof}
 
\begin{ex}\label{ex:epi}
 Given a map of \'etale sheaves $F\to G$,  show it is a surjection if
and only if $G$ is the coequalizer of the pair of maps
$F\x_GF\rightrightarrows F$.
 \end{ex}

\begin{ex}\label{ex:q-proj}
 Assume $X/S$ is projective and flat, its geometric fibers are integral,
and $S$ is Noetherian.  Let $Z\subset \IPic_{X/S}$ be a subscheme of
finite type.  Show $Z$ is quasi-projective.

---
name: leansearch
description: Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
---

**Search before you prove.** Most facts you need already exist in mathlib or the
workspace. Searching is far cheaper than reproving. Use the local index first
(unlimited, instant), then the LSP search tools for broader semantic/type search.

## Local first: `horizon search`

An offline declaration search over `external_libraries` (mathlib by default) plus
the workspace's own projects. No GPU, API key, or network. Three modes share one
cached index:

- Natural language — what a lemma says:
  `horizon search "continuous function on a compact set attains its maximum"`
- `--name` — find a declaration by partial name:
  `horizon search --name isCompact.image`
- `--type` — find by shape of the statement; `?a`/`?b`/`_` are wildcards:
  `horizon search --type "Continuous ?f -> IsCompact ?s -> IsCompact (?f '' ?s)"`

Useful flags: `-n K`, `--lib NAME`, `--json`, `--reindex`. If results look thin,
run the project build so sources are current, then `horizon search --reindex`.

## Lean LSP MCP search tools

The `lean-lsp` MCP server (configured in `.mcp.json`) exposes a full search
arsenal. Rate limits are **per-tool** (separate pools), not a shared budget.

| Tool | Use it for | Limit |
|------|-----------|-------|
| `lean_local_search` | exact/partial declaration name; workspace + mathlib | unlimited |
| `lean_leansearch` | **semantic search by mathematical meaning** (PKU LeanSearch) | 10 / 30s |
| `lean_loogle` | search by **type shape** when you know the signature, not the name | remote; unlimited in `--loogle-local` |
| `lean_state_search` | lemmas that apply to a specific **proof state** (goal at a line) | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_hammer_premise` | **premise names** to feed `simp only [...]` / `aesop` / `grind` | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_leanfinder` | semantic fallback — only when `lean_leansearch` fails | 10 / 30s |

### Priority / escalation order

1. `lean_local_search("name")` — always first; unlimited, instant, deterministic.
2. `lean_leansearch("describe the math.")` — primary semantic search (see below).
3. `lean_loogle("?a -> ?b")` — simple type patterns only.
4. `lean_state_search(file, line, col)` — goal-conditioned lookup when stuck.
5. `lean_hammer_premise(file, line, col)` — premises for `simp`/`aesop`/`grind`.
6. `lean_leanfinder("description")` — last-resort semantic fallback.

### `lean_leansearch` — the PKU semantic tool (use it well)

LeanSearch (leansearch.net, from the PKU team) augments each mathlib theorem into
an informal description and matches your query against those embeddings —
returning the **nearest neighbours**, not just exact hits. That is its strength:
a theorem 90% of what you need is often enough; prove the small gap yourself.

- **Describe the mathematical content, not the name.** Query must end with `.`/`?`.
  - Good: `lean_leansearch("The image of a compact set under a continuous map is compact.")`
  - Good (mixed): `lean_leansearch("natural numbers. from: n < m, to: n + 1 < m + 1")`
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("add_comm")` → use `lean_local_search` instead.
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("∀ (a b : ℕ), a + b = b + a")` → use `lean_loogle` instead.
- **Trust a negative result.** If a precise, mathematically accurate description
  returns nothing relevant, the theorem likely isn't in mathlib — stop rephrasing
  and prove it (or find another route) rather than searching endlessly.

### `lean_loogle` — type-shape search

Searches by *type structure*, not names. Syntax: `?a`/`?b` type vars, `_`
wildcards, `->`/`→` arrows, `|- pattern` by conclusion.
- Good: `lean_loogle("(?a -> ?b) -> List ?a -> List ?b")` → `List.map`
- Anti-pattern: nested `Submodule`/`LinearMap`/`Finsupp`, 3+ typeclass
  constraints, or guessy implicit structure — use `lean_leansearch` for those.

## Discipline

- Treat every hit as a **candidate**: read the signature/source and confirm with
  the Lean checker (see the `lean-check` skill) before depending on it.
- Try multiple phrasings — project name, mathematical concept, conclusion/type.
- Local (`horizon search` / `lean_local_search`) is optimized for the checked-out
  sources here; the LSP tools reach broader mathlib precedent. Use both.

---
name: hgraph
description: The dependency graph — Horizon's vendored hgraph core keeps one file per statement/Lean declaration under <project>/hgraph/; `horizon graph frontier` ranks work and agents attach node-scoped comments and reviews. This is the only DAG engine.
---

Each project may carry an **hgraph**: a plain-files semantic graph under
`<project>/hgraph/` — one Markdown node per blueprint statement and per Lean
declaration, typed edges (`uses` = the hard dependency DAG, `formalizes` =
informal↔formal identity). `horizon graph sync` (run automatically at run boundaries)
reconciles the blueprint + Lean sources into it; your **authored** additions
(comments, reviews, metadata) are never touched by sync. The files are
committed to the workspace ledger like everything else.

Use `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …`; when a workspace has one project,
`-p` is optional. Address nodes by `label:<latex-label>` or
`decl:<lean-fqname>` — raw ids are opaque hashes. Most commands accept `--json`.

## Sync it yourself — and act on the warnings

Don't wait for the run boundary: after you change blueprint statements,
`\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations, or Lean declarations, run
`"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> sync` and **read its output**. Sync prints warnings for exactly the defects
you can fix on the spot: `\uses{X} has no blueprint node` (missing/mistyped
label), `\lean{Name} not found in Lean sources` (renamed or unwritten
declaration), stale nodes whose source vanished. Fix what your change caused
before moving on; a warning you deliberately leave (e.g. a forward reference
you'll write next) gets a node comment or a memory item so the next session
knows it's intentional. Sync is idempotent and never touches your authored
comments/reviews/metadata.

## Read

- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> list --state ready` — nodes whose dependencies are all closed:
  provable *now*. Other states: `closed`, `blocked`, `formalized_open`.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` — the ready nodes ranked by how many downstream nodes a
  proof would unlock. **Use this when picking the next node to prove.**
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:thm:foo` — one node: statement, `lean_status`
  (`lean_ok | mathlib_ok | sorry | empty`, derived from scanning the Lean, not
  from `\leanok`), deps, attached comments/reviews.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> ancestors label:thm:foo` — the dependency cone.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> stats` — per-state counts for the project.

## Write — per-node progress lives WITH the node

- **Comment = failure memory / progress note on that node.** When an approach
  fails or you learn something node-specific, record it where the next session
  will look first:
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add comment label:thm:foo --content "tried simp+ring, fails because …"`
  Agent authorship plus run/session/task provenance are filled from the run
  environment; do not copy the note into the blueprint.
- **Review = a Maths / Lean verdict** (independent axes, `good|bad`):
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add review label:thm:foo --maths good --lean bad --lean-comment "statement ok; proof has a sorry at the succ case"`
- **Metadata**: `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> modify node label:thm:foo --set status=verified`

Prefer node comments over inbox items for anything scoped to ONE node; use the
inbox (skill: `horizon-inbox`) for cross-node or cross-session coordination.

An edge `source --uses--> target` means *source depends on target*. A node is
"ready" when all of its dependencies are closed; prefer `frontier`, which ranks
ready nodes by what they unlock. The dashboard provides the workspace project
switcher and the chapter-collapsed Graphviz view.

## Relation to the blueprint

The DAG **is** the hgraph — there is no second engine and no parser fallback.
It is generated by resolving the blueprint's `\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations
against the real Lean sources, so keeping those annotations correct (skill:
`blueprint-conventions`) is exactly what keeps this graph correct. Unresolved
references surface as `horizon graph sync` warnings and as `dangling` entries — read
the warnings rather than trusting `dangling` alone.

---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSheafification
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjective
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The admissible Abel quotient in big-etale sheaves
    11	
    12	Etale-local surjectivity of the concrete admissible Abel transformation makes its image
    13	the full sheafified Picard Sigma target. Consequently that target is the effective
    14	coequalizer of the map's kernel pair in big-etale sheaves.
    15	
    16	This is not yet a quotient in `Scheme`: representing the kernel pair by a scheme, proving
    17	effectivity of its geometric quotient, and identifying `pic0SigmaEtaleSheafification C`
    18	with the original `pic0TypeFunctor C` remain separate steps.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    26	
    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    28	
    29	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    32	
    33	/-- The sheafified concrete admissible Abel map is locally surjective on the big-etale
    34	site. -/
    35	instance admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap_isLocallySurjective :
    36	    Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C) := by
    37	  letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.etaleTopology
    38	      (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C) :=
    39	    isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C
    40	  letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.etaleTopology
    41	      (Functor.whiskerRight (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C)
    42	        uliftFunctor.{u + 1}) :=
    43	    Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_whiskerRight_ulift
    44	      Scheme.etaleTopology (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C)
    45	  haveI : Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
    46	      ((presheafToSheaf Scheme.etaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).map
    47	        (Functor.whiskerRight (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C)
    48	          uliftFunctor.{u + 1})) :=
    49	    (Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_presheafToSheaf_map_iff
    50	      Scheme.etaleTopology _).2 inferInstance
    51	  haveI : Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
    52	      (admissibleAbelEtaleSourceIso C).hom := by infer_instance
    53	  exact Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_comp
    54	    (admissibleAbelEtaleSourceIso C).hom
    55	    ((presheafToSheaf Scheme.etaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).map
    56	      (Functor.whiskerRight (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C)
    57	        uliftFunctor.{u + 1}))
    58	
    59	/-- The image of the sheafified admissible Abel map is the full sheafified Picard Sigma
    60	target. -/
    61	noncomputable def admissibleAbelEtaleImageIsoTarget :
    62	    admissibleAbelEtaleImage C ≅ pic0SigmaEtaleSheafification C := by
    63	  haveI : IsIso (Sheaf.imageι (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)) :=
    64	    (Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_isIso _).mp inferInstance
    65	  exact asIso (Sheaf.imageι (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C))
    66	
    67	/-- The full sheafified Picard Sigma target is the effective coequalizer of the kernel
    68	pair of the concrete admissible Abel map. -/
    69	noncomputable def admissibleAbelEtaleTargetCoequalizer :
    70	    IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
    71	      (IsKernelPair.of_hasPullback (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)).w) := by
    72	  haveI : IsRegularEpi (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C) :=
    73	    IsRegularEpiCategory.regularEpiOfEpi _
    74	  exact (IsKernelPair.of_hasPullback
    75	    (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)).toCoequalizer'
    76	
    77	end AlgebraicGeometry

     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.

     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelKernel
     7	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Proetale
     8	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.LocallyBijective
     9	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.RegularEpi
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# The admissible Abel map after big-etale sheafification
    13	
    14	The big etale site of `Scheme.{u}` requires type-valued sheafification in `Type (u + 1)`.
    15	This module therefore applies `ULift` to the concrete admissible Abel transformation before
    16	sheafifying it. Subcanonicity identifies the sheafified source with the actual representable
    17	Yoneda sheaf of `divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C`.
    18	
    19	The target here is deliberately the etale sheafification of `pic0SigmaFunctor C`; identifying
    20	it with the original Picard functor is a separate mathematical step. The categorical image
    21	of the Abel map is the effective quotient of its kernel pair in the category of etale sheaves.
    22	No Scheme representability conclusion is asserted in this module.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	set_option autoImplicit false
    26	
    27	universe u v w w'
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    30	
    31	namespace CategoryTheory.Presheaf
    32	
    33	variable {X : Type u} [Category.{v} X] (J : GrothendieckTopology X)
    34	
    35	/-- Local surjectivity of a type-valued presheaf map survives a universe lift. -/
    36	theorem isLocallySurjective_whiskerRight_ulift
    37	    {F G : Xᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (f : F ⟶ G)
    38	    [IsLocallySurjective J f] :
    39	    IsLocallySurjective J
    40	      (Functor.whiskerRight f uliftFunctor.{w', w}) := by
    41	  constructor
    42	  intro U s
    43	  apply J.superset_covering _ (imageSieve_mem J f s.down)
    44	  intro V i hi
    45	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hi
    46	  refine ⟨ULift.up t, ?_⟩
    47	  apply ULift.ext
    48	  exact ht
    49	
    50	end CategoryTheory.Presheaf
    51	
    52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    53	
    54	/-! ## Subcanonicity of the big etale site -/
    55	
    56	/-- The big etale topology on schemes is subcanonical. -/
    57	instance Scheme.subcanonical_etaleTopology : Scheme.etaleTopology.{u}.Subcanonical :=
    58	  GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology
    59	
    60	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    61	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    62	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    63	
    64	/-! ## The sheafified concrete Abel map -/
    65	
    66	/-- The big-etale sheafification of the universe-raised Picard Sigma presheaf. -/
    67	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaEtaleSheafification :
    68	    Sheaf Scheme.etaleTopology.{u} (Type (u + 1)) :=
    69	  (presheafToSheaf Scheme.etaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).obj
    70	    (pic0SigmaFunctor C ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1})
    71	
    72	/-- Subcanonicity identifies the universe-raised Yoneda sheaf of the admissible divisor
    73	representer with the sheafification of its underlying representable presheaf. -/
    74	noncomputable def admissibleAbelEtaleSourceIso :
    75	    Scheme.etaleTopology.uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj
    76	        (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ≅
    77	      (presheafToSheaf Scheme.etaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).obj
    78	        (yoneda.obj (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1}) :=
    79	  (asIso ((sheafificationAdjunction Scheme.etaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).counit.app
    80	    (Scheme.etaleTopology.uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj
    81	      (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left))).symm
    82	
    83	/-- The concrete admissible Abel transformation as a morphism from its representable
    84	big-etale Yoneda source to the sheafification of the Picard Sigma presheaf. -/
    85	noncomputable def admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap :
    86	    Scheme.etaleTopology.uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj
    87	        (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ⟶
    88	      pic0SigmaEtaleSheafification C :=
    89	  (admissibleAbelEtaleSourceIso C).hom ≫
    90	    (presheafToSheaf Scheme.etaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).map
    91	      (Functor.whiskerRight (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C) uliftFunctor.{u + 1})
    92	
    93	/-! ## The effective image quotient in etale sheaves -/
    94	
    95	/-- The image sheaf of the concrete admissible Abel map. -/
    96	noncomputable abbrev admissibleAbelEtaleImage :
    97	    Sheaf Scheme.etaleTopology.{u} (Type (u + 1)) :=
    98	  Sheaf.image (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
    99	
   100	/-- The canonical epimorphism from the admissible divisor source to the Abel image sheaf. -/
   101	noncomputable abbrev admissibleAbelEtaleToImage :
   102	    Scheme.etaleTopology.uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj
   103	        (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ⟶
   104	      admissibleAbelEtaleImage C :=
   105	  Sheaf.toImage (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
   106	
   107	/-- The kernel pair of the map onto the Abel image is the pullback kernel pair of the original
   108	concrete Abel sheaf map. -/
   109	noncomputable def admissibleAbelEtaleImageKernelPair :
   110	    IsKernelPair (admissibleAbelEtaleToImage C)

   118	      (pullback.fst (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
   119	        (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C))
   120	      (pullback.snd (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
   121	        (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)) := by

    10	/-!
    11	# The widened divisor representer at the Picard atlas seam
    12	
    13	The widened divisor functor of a challenge curve is represented at the genus parameter.  This
    14	module inserts that representation into the Abel construction and then into the Zariski-local
    15	representability theorem for the degree-zero Picard functor.
    16	
    17	The resulting chart family has no assumed divisor representation.  Its remaining inputs are the
    18	two geometric conditions of the local-representability theorem: every restricted Abel map is a
    19	representable open immersion, and the restricted maps cover the Picard sheaf pointwise.
    20	
    21	This is not an unconditional Picard representability result: the final declaration below retains
    22	both geometric inputs.  Moreover, at the larger admissible coverage parameter the raw Abel map has
    23	positive-dimensional linear-system fibres in positive genus, so the larger divisor representer
    24	cannot simply be substituted as an open chart source.  The remaining datum-tail construction is
    25	the corrected Altman--Kleiman step: represent the quotient by equality of the induced Picard class,
    26	thereby removing those fibres before applying the Picard representability seam.
    27	
    28	## Main declarations
    29	
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffGenus` is the widened Abel chart formed from the chosen
    31	  genus-parameter divisor representer.
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.universalDivFamAffGenus` is its universal widened divisor family.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible` is the no-argument widened Abel map at the
    34	  unconditional admissible coverage parameter; its legal chart index is chosen internally.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.universalDivFamAffAdmissible` is the corresponding universal family.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineGenusChart` restricts a multi-index family of these maps to chosen
    37	  source opens.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts` is the conditional final assembly
    39	  once the restricted charts are open immersions and cover pointwise.
    40	-/
    41	
    42	set_option autoImplicit false
    43	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    44	
    45	universe u
    46	
    47	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
    48	
    49	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    50	
    51	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    52	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    53	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    54	
    55	noncomputable section
    56	
    57	/-- The universal widened divisor family carried by the chosen genus-parameter representer. -/
    58	def universalDivFamAffGenus :
    59	    divFamZarAff C (genus C) (divRepAffGenusScheme C) :=
    60	  (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv (𝟙 _)
    61	
    62	/-- Pulling back the chosen universal family gives the widened family classified by the
    63	corresponding morphism into the genus representer. -/
    64	theorem universalDivFamAffGenus_map {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    65	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
    66	    divFamZarAff.map C (genus C) q (universalDivFamAffGenus C)
    67	      = (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q := by
    68	  have h := (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp q
    69	    (𝟙 (divRepAffGenusScheme C))
    70	  rw [Category.comp_id] at h
    71	  exact h.symm
    72	
    73	/-- The universal widened divisor family carried by the unconditional representer at the
    74	admissible coverage parameter. -/
    75	def universalDivFamAffAdmissible :
    76	    divFamZarAff C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :=
    77	  (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv (𝟙 _)
    78	
    79	/-- Pullback of the admissible universal family agrees with classification by the unconditional
    80	admissible representer. -/

    82	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :
    83	    divFamZarAff.map C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) q
    84	        (universalDivFamAffAdmissible C)
    85	      = (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q := by
    86	  have h := (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp q
    87	    (𝟙 (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C))
    88	  rw [Category.comp_id] at h
    89	  exact h.symm

    91	/-- The widened Abel chart at the genus parameter, using the challenge curve's chosen divisor
    92	representer rather than accepting a representability witness as an argument. -/
    93	def abelSigmaChartAffGenus
    94	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    95	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    96	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ)) :
    97	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
    98	  abelSigmaChartAff C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg

   100	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra in
   101	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver in
   102	/-- The widened Abel map at the unconditional admissible coverage parameter.  A legal chart
   103	index whose locus is universal is chosen internally; this declaration does not assert that the
   104	raw Abel map is an open immersion or an atlas. -/
   105	def abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible :
   106	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 := by
   107	  classical
   108	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
   109	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   110	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
   111	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
   112	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   113	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
   114	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
   115	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
   116	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
   117	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
   118	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
   119	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
   120	  let hchart := exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ
   121	    (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C) (chi_moduleKSheaf C)
   122	  let m : ℕ := Classical.choose hchart
   123	  let hZ := Classical.choose_spec hchart
   124	  let Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor := Classical.choose hZ
   125	  have hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   126	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
   127	        - (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ) := by
   128	    change Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   129	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
   130	        - (admissibleCoverageParameter
   131	            (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C) : ℤ)
   132	    exact (Classical.choose_spec hZ).1
   133	  exact abelSigmaChartAff C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)
   134	    (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C) m Z hdeg

   136	/-- The structure morphism read from a genus-parameter widened Abel chart is the structure
   137	morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
   138	lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus
   139	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   140	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   141	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   142	    {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
   143	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAffGenus C m Z hdeg) i
   144	      = (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom :=
   145	  chartHom_abelSigmaChartAff (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg i
   146	
   147	/-- The structure morphism read from the admissible Abel map is the structure morphism of the
   148	unconditional admissible divisor representer. -/
   149	lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
   150	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C) i
   151	      = (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom := by
   152	  dsimp only [abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible]
   153	  exact chartHom_abelSigmaChartAff
   154	    (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C) _ _ _ i
   155	
   156	/-- A multi-index family of genus-parameter widened Abel charts, restricted to source opens.
   157	Different indices may use different twists and different opens, but they all use the same
   158	unconditional divisor representer. -/
   159	def affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
   160	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   161	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   162	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   163	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
   164	    yoneda.obj (V i : Scheme) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
   165	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
   166	
   167	/-- The structure morphism of a restricted genus chart is the inclusion of its source open
   168	followed by the structure morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
   169	lemma chartHom_affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
   170	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   171	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   172	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   173	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
   174	    chartHom C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) i
   175	      = (V i).ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom := by
   176	  have hrestrict := chartHom_restrictChart (C := C)
   177	    (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i) i
   178	  have hgenus := chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) i
   179	  simpa only [chartHom, affineGenusChart] using
   180	    hrestrict.trans (congrArg ((V i).ι ≫ ·) hgenus)
   181	
   182	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor is represented by the glued object of any pointwise-covering
   183	family of open genus-parameter widened Abel charts.
   184	
   185	The divisor representation is construction data, not a hypothesis: it is supplied by
   186	`divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy`.  The two hypotheses are exactly the geometric inputs of
   187	Zariski local representability. -/
   188	def pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts {ι : Type u}
   189	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   190	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   191	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   192	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens)
   193	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V i))
   194	    (hcov : PointwiseCoverage C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :
   195	    Σ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J := by
   196	  letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
   197	      (Sigma.desc (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :=
   198	    isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ hcov
   199	  exact ⟨_, pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) hf⟩
   200

    15	relation with the quotient by `picFromBase`.

    18	divisor representer must represent.  No quotient scheme or representability conclusion is
    19	asserted here.

    50	/-- Equality of widened Abel values is equality of their relative Picard classes on every

    52	theorem abelDivAff'_eq_iff_forall_relPicMk_picClass_eq
    53	    [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
    54	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (s₁ s₂ : divFamZarAff C n T) :
    55	    abelDivAff' C n T s₁ = abelDivAff' C n T s₂

   177	theorem abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_eq_sigmaExtension_admissibleAbelTrans :

   189	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :

   196	/-- The kernel of the concrete admissible Abel transformation is precisely relative linear

   199	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q₁ q₂ : T ⟶ divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :

   203	              (((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₂).1 U).picClass
   204	            ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) := by
   205	  unfold admissibleAbelTrans admissibleChartValueAffTrans
   206	  constructor
   207	  · intro h
   208	    apply (chartValueAff_eq_iff_forall_picClass_div_mem_picFromBase C
   209	      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (admissibleAbelChartIndex C)
   210	        (admissibleAbelChartDivisor C) T
   211	          ((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₁)
   212	          ((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₂)).mp
   213	    exact congrArg Subtype.val h

   216	    exact (chartValueAff_eq_iff_forall_picClass_div_mem_picFromBase C
   217	      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (admissibleAbelChartIndex C)
   218	        (admissibleAbelChartDivisor C) T

   223	/-- Evaluation of the ambient admissible Sigma chart on the left leg of a slice point is the
   224	same slice Abel value, transported to the point's actual structure morphism. -/
   225	theorem abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_app_left
   226	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   227	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :
   228	    (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C).app (op T.left) q.left =
   229	      (⟨T.hom, (admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q⟩ :
   230	        (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T.left)) := by
   231	  rw [abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_eq_sigmaExtension_admissibleAbelTrans]
   232	  change (⟨q.left ≫ (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom, _⟩ :
   233	      (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T.left)) =
   234	    ⟨T.hom, (admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q⟩
   235	  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C) q.w ?_
   236	  let e : Over.mk (q.left ≫ (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom) ⟶ T :=
   237	    Over.mkCongr q.w
   238	  let q' : Over.mk (q.left ≫ (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom) ⟶
   239	      divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C :=
   240	    Over.homMk q.left rfl
   241	  have hq : e ≫ q = q' := by
   242	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   243	    exact Category.id_comp _
   244	  change (pic0TypeFunctor C).map e.op
   245	      ((admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q) =
   246	    (admissibleAbelTrans C).app
   247	      (op (Over.mk (q.left ≫ (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom))) q'
   248	  have hnat := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
   249	    ((admissibleAbelTrans C).naturality e.op) q
   250	  have hmap : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C)).map e.op q = q' := by
   251	    exact hq
   252	  simpa only [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, hmap] using hnat.symm

   258	theorem abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_app_left_eq_iff_forall_picClass_div_mem_picFromBase

   262	        (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C).app (op T.left) q₂.left
   263	      ↔ ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
   264	          (((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₁).1 U).picClass /
   265	              (((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₂).1 U).picClass
   266	            ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) := by
   267	  rw [abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_app_left C q₁,
   268	    abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_app_left C q₂]
   269	  change (⟨T.hom, (admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q₁⟩ :
   270	      (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T.left)) =
   271	        ⟨T.hom, (admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q₂⟩ ↔ _
   272	  rw [Sigma.mk.inj_iff]

     9	/-!
    10	# The concrete project-local model of the admissible divisor representer
    11	
    12	The admissible coverage parameter is strictly positive, so the chosen representer in
    13	`DivRepAffChallenge` is definitionally the nonzero `DivScheme` branch.  This file names that
    14	concrete branch and transports its closed immersion into the Grassmannian pair back to
    15	`divRepAffAdmissibleScheme`.
    16	
    17	The resulting certificate is unconditional and geometric: the target has its finite affine
    18	product atlas, and the source is quasi-compact, locally of finite type, and separated over the
    19	base field.  It is not yet a finite-projective-space immersion.  That stronger conclusion needs
    20	the Plucker embeddings of both Grassmannian factors together with their Segre product; those
    21	maps are not present in the rebuild project.

    99	  have hM := windowBound_le_M_mul

    12	/-!
    13	# H-quasi-projectivity transport for Grassmannian representers
    14	
    15	This file isolates the transport needed by the D4' divisor route. An
    16	H-quasi-projectivity certificate for the absolute Grassmannian over `Spec Z`
    17	base-changes to the explicit relative free Grassmannian. Over a field, a
    18	locally free module is globally free, so uniqueness of representing objects
    19	then transports the certificate to the chosen `Scheme.Grassmannian`
    20	representer.
    21	
    22	The absolute certificate is constructed by the Plucker embedding in
    23	`Projective/GrassmannianProjective.lean`. The conditional transport theorem is
    24	retained to isolate the base-change argument, and the unconditional theorem at
    25	the end consumes the absolute certificate.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	namespace Scheme
    34	namespace Grassmannian
    35	
    36	private noncomputable def pullbackTopFreeIso {T : Scheme.{0}}
    37	    (N : T.Modules) (I : Type)
    38	    (e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (⊤ : T.Opens).ι).obj N ≅
    39	      SheafOfModules.free (R := (⊤ : T.Opens).toScheme.ringCatSheaf) I) :
    40	    N ≅ SheafOfModules.free (R := T.ringCatSheaf) I :=
    41	  (Scheme.Modules.pullbackTopIsoSelf N).symm ≪≫
    42	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback T.topIso.inv).mapIso e ≪≫
    43	    Scheme.Modules.pullbackFreeIso T.topIso.inv I
    44	
    45	private theorem globallyFreeSpecField {K : Type} [Field K]
    46	    {V : (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).Modules} {r : ℕ}
    47	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r) :
    48	    Nonempty (V ≅ SheafOfModules.free
    49	      (R := (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).ringCatSheaf) (Fin r)) := by
    50	  let S : Scheme.{0} := Spec (CommRingCat.of K)
    51	  obtain ⟨ι, U, hU, htriv⟩ := hV
    52	  let x : S := Classical.arbitrary S
    53	  have hx : x ∈ ⨆ i, U i := by rw [hU]; trivial
    54	  rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup] at hx
    55	  obtain ⟨i, hxi⟩ := hx
    56	  let W : S.Opens := U i
    57	  have hxW : x ∈ W := hxi
    58	  have hW : W = ⊤ := Scheme.Opens.eq_top_of_subsingleton W hxW
    59	  have htrivW : Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback W.ι).obj V ≅
    60	      SheafOfModules.free (R := W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
    61	        (ULift.{0} (Fin r))) := htriv i
    62	  clear_value W
    63	  subst W
    64	  obtain ⟨e⟩ := htrivW
    65	  refine ⟨pullbackTopFreeIso V _ e ≪≫ ?_⟩
    66	  exact (SheafOfModules.freeFunctor (R := S.ringCatSheaf)).mapIso
    67	    (Equiv.toIso Equiv.ulift)
    68	
    69	private theorem productHQuasiProjectiveOfAbsolute (d r : ℕ)
    70	    (habs : (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.toSpecZ d r).IsHQuasiProjective)
    71	    (S : Scheme.{0}) :
    72	    (((Over.star S).obj
    73	      (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.scheme d r)).hom).IsHQuasiProjective := by
    74	  let G : Scheme.{0} := AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.scheme d r
    75	  let hc : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk
    76	      (prod.snd : S ⨯ G ⟶ G) (prod.fst : S ⨯ G ⟶ S)
    77	      (specZIsTerminal.hom_ext
    78	        ((prod.snd : S ⨯ G ⟶ G) ≫
    79	          AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.toSpecZ d r)
    80	        ((prod.fst : S ⨯ G ⟶ S) ≫ specZIsTerminal.from S))) :=
    81	    isPullbackOfIsTerminalIsProduct
    82	      (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.toSpecZ d r)
    83	      (specZIsTerminal.from S)
    84	      (prod.snd : S ⨯ G ⟶ G) (prod.fst : S ⨯ G ⟶ S)
    85	      specZIsTerminal (prodIsProd S G).binaryFanSwap
    86	  let e : (S ⨯ G) ≅ pullback
    87	      (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.toSpecZ d r)
    88	      (specZIsTerminal.from S) :=
    89	    hc.conePointUniqueUpToIso (limit.isLimit _)
    90	  have he : e.hom ≫ pullback.snd
    91	      (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.toSpecZ d r)
    92	      (specZIsTerminal.from S) = (prod.fst : S ⨯ G ⟶ S) :=
    93	    hc.conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom_comp
    94	      (limit.isLimit _) WalkingCospan.right
    95	  have hprod : (prod.fst : S ⨯ G ⟶ S).IsHQuasiProjective := by
    96	    rw [← he]
    97	    exact (habs.baseChange (specZIsTerminal.from S)).comp_isImmersion e.hom
    98	  change (prod.lift prod.fst (𝟙 (S ⨯ G)) ≫
    99	    prod.fst).IsHQuasiProjective
   100	  rw [prod.lift_fst]
   101	  exact hprod
   102	
   103	/-- Over a field, H-quasi-projectivity of the absolute Grassmannian transports
   104	to the chosen scheme representing locally free rank-`d` quotients of `V`.
   105	
   106	This theorem isolates the exact reduction used by D4'. Its only projective
   107	input is the certificate for `Grassmannian.toSpecZ`; no explicit
   108	`RepresentableBy` witness is added to the consumer signature. -/
   109	theorem representingScheme_isHQuasiProjective_of_field_of_absolute
   110	    {K : Type} [Field K]
   111	    {V : (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).Modules} {r d : ℕ}
   112	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r)
   113	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r)
   114	    (habs : (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.toSpecZ d r).IsHQuasiProjective) :
   115	    (representingScheme hV hd hdr).hom.IsHQuasiProjective := by
   116	  obtain ⟨eV⟩ := globallyFreeSpecField hV
   117	  let S : Scheme.{0} := Spec (CommRingCat.of K)
   118	  let Y : Over S := (Over.star S).obj
   119	    (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.scheme d r)
   120	  let repY : (Scheme.Grassmannian V d).RepresentableBy Y :=
   121	    (prodRepresentableBy S d r hd hdr).ofIso
   122	      ((Scheme.Grassmannian.congrIso eV d ≪≫ freeCompare d r).symm)
   123	  let E : representingScheme hV hd hdr ≅ Y :=
   124	    (representation hV hd hdr).uniqueUpToIso repY
   125	  rw [← E.hom.w]
   126	  exact (productHQuasiProjectiveOfAbsolute d r habs S).comp_isImmersion
   127	    E.hom.left
   128	
   129	/-- Over a field, the chosen scheme representing locally free rank-`d`
   130	quotients of `V` is H-quasi-projective. -/
   131	theorem representingScheme_isHQuasiProjective_of_field
   132	    {K : Type} [Field K]
   133	    {V : (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).Modules} {r d : ℕ}
   134	    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r)
   135	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :
   136	    (representingScheme hV hd hdr).hom.IsHQuasiProjective := by
   137	  exact representingScheme_isHQuasiProjective_of_field_of_absolute hV hd hdr
   138	    (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.isHQuasiProjective_toSpecZ d r)
   139	
   140	end Grassmannian
   141	end Scheme
   142	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveSpace
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Projective and H-quasi-projective morphisms
    10	
    11	This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that
    12	Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide. A morphism is projective when it factors as
    13	a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.
    14	
    15	A morphism is **H-quasi-projective** when it factors through a quasi-compact
    16	immersion into such a projective space, following the finite-projective-space
    17	convention of [Stacks, Tag 01VV].  The quasi-compactness is part of the
    18	definition: without it the predicate only records an immersion/relative very
    19	ampleness and need not imply finite type.  This predicate is not asserted to
    20	be equivalent over arbitrary bases to every formulation using relative ample
    21	line bundles.  Both predicates are stable under base change.
    22	
    23	The line-bundle-carrying refinement used by the Quot construction remains in
    24	`Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean`; that refinement is universe-monomorphic because
    25	its Serre twist is built by the project-local sheaf gluing engine.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	universe u
    33	
    34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    35	
    36	/-- A morphism is projective if it admits a closed immersion into a
    37	finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    38	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    39	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    40	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    41	
    42	/-- A morphism is H-quasi-projective if it admits a quasi-compact immersion into
    43	a finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    44	def Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    45	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    46	    IsImmersion i ∧ QuasiCompact i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    47	
    48	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    49	
    50	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    51	
    52	/-- A projective morphism is H-quasi-projective. -/
    53	theorem isHQuasiProjective (h : pi.IsProjective) : pi.IsHQuasiProjective := by
    54	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    55	  letI : Finite n := hn
    56	  haveI : IsClosedImmersion i := hi
    57	  exact ⟨n, hn, i, inferInstance, inferInstance, hcomp⟩
    58	
    59	/-- Projective morphisms are proper. -/
    60	theorem isProper (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsProper pi := by
    61	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    62	  letI : Finite n := hn
    63	  haveI := hi
    64	  rw [← hcomp]
    65	  infer_instance
    66	
    67	/-- Projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
    68	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi :=
    69	  haveI := h.isProper
    70	  inferInstance
    71	
    72	/-- Projective morphisms are separated. -/
    73	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsSeparated pi :=
    74	  haveI := h.isProper
    75	  inferInstance
    76	
    77	/-- Projective morphisms are universally closed. -/
    78	theorem universallyClosed (h : pi.IsProjective) : UniversallyClosed pi :=
    79	  haveI := h.isProper
    80	  inferInstance
    81	
    82	/-- A closed immersion into a projective scheme is projective. -/
    83	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : pi.IsProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    84	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] : (j ≫ pi).IsProjective := by
    85	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    86	  letI : Finite n := hn
    87	  haveI := hi
    88	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
    89	
    90	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed source to the corresponding
    91	base change of its ambient projective space. -/
    92	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
    93	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
    94	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
    95	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
    96	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
    97	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
    98	
    99	/-- Projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
   100	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
   101	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsProjective := by
   102	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
   103	  letI : Finite n := hn
   104	  haveI := hi
   105	  refine ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_⟩
   106	  · have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
   107	        pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   108	    have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
   109	        (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
   110	      have hbig : IsPullback
   111	          (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
   112	          (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
   113	        rw [h1, hcomp]
   114	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
   115	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
   116	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
   117	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
   118	    exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi
   119	  · exact IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   120	
   121	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
   122	
   123	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective
   124	
   125	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
   126	
   127	/-- H-quasi-projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
   128	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi := by
   129	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, _, hcomp⟩ := h
   130	  letI : Finite n := hn
   131	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   132	  rw [← hcomp]
   133	  infer_instance
   134	
   135	/-- H-quasi-projective morphisms are quasi-compact. -/
   136	theorem quasiCompact (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) : QuasiCompact pi := by
   137	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h
   138	  letI : Finite n := hn
   139	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   140	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc
   141	  rw [← hcomp]
   142	  infer_instance
   143	
   144	/-- H-quasi-projective morphisms are separated. -/
   145	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) : IsSeparated pi := by
   146	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, _, hcomp⟩ := h
   147	  letI : Finite n := hn
   148	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   149	  rw [← hcomp]
   150	  infer_instance
   151	
   152	/-- A quasi-compact immersion into an H-quasi-projective scheme is
   153	H-quasi-projective. -/
   154	theorem comp_isImmersion (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
   155	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j] :
   156	    (j ≫ pi).IsHQuasiProjective := by
   157	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h
   158	  letI : Finite n := hn
   159	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   160	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc
   161	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
   162	
   163	/-- The comparison from a base-changed source to the corresponding base change
   164	of its ambient projective space. -/
   165	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
   166	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
   167	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
   168	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
   169	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
   170	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
   171	
   172	/-- H-quasi-projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
   173	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsHQuasiProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
   174	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsHQuasiProjective := by
   175	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hqc, hcomp⟩ := h
   176	  letI : Finite n := hn
   177	  haveI : IsImmersion i := hi
   178	  haveI : QuasiCompact i := hqc
   179	  have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
   180	      pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   181	  have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
   182	      (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
   183	    have hbig : IsPullback
   184	        (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
   185	        (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
   186	      rw [h1, hcomp]
   187	      exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
   188	    exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
   189	      (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
   190	      (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
   191	  exact ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp,
   192	    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi,
   193	    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hqc, h1⟩
   194	
   195	end Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective
   196	
   197	namespace ProjectiveSpace
   198	
   199	/-- The structural morphism of relative projective space is projective. -/
   200	theorem isProjective_over (n : Type u) [Finite n] (S : Scheme.{u}) :
   201	    (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S).IsProjective :=
   202	  ⟨n, inferInstance, 𝟙 _, inferInstance, Category.id_comp _⟩
   203	
   204	/-- The structural morphism of relative projective space is H-quasi-projective. -/
   205	theorem isHQuasiProjective_over (n : Type u) [Finite n] (S : Scheme.{u}) :
   206	    (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S).IsHQuasiProjective :=
   207	  (isProjective_over n S).isHQuasiProjective
   208	
   209	end ProjectiveSpace
   210	
   211	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!

    15	local finite-typeness over `k`, and separatedness, and the same three properties derived
    16	on `DivScheme g` itself (closed immersions into qc/lft/separated transfer).
    17	
    18	## The Grassmannian-pair data (§4.1 middle factor)
    19	
    20	* `Grassmannian.isAffine_grPairCover_X`: each patch of the finite product atlas
    21	  `grPairCover` is affine (with `finite_grPairCover_index`, `GrassmannianPair.lean:68`:
    22	  the **finite affine frame atlas**).
    23	* `Grassmannian.compactSpace_grPair`, `quasiCompact_grPairStructMap`: quasi-compactness
    24	  is FREE — finitely many affine charts glue to a compact space; no image argument.
    25	* `Grassmannian.locallyOfFiniteType_grPairStructMap`: charts are `Spec` of finite-type
    26	  `k`-algebras (DD-3's `locallyOfFiniteType_grStructMap`), stable under base change and
    27	  composition through the pair.
    28	* `Grassmannian.isSeparated_grPairStructMap`, `isSeparated_grPair`: the GRQ
    29	  affine-diagonal argument (DD-3's `isSeparated_grStructMap`) through the pullback.
    30	
    31	## The derived bundle on `DivScheme g` (§4.2 consumer rows)
    32	
    33	* `quasiCompact_carveSchemeOverHom` / `quasiCompact_divSchemeOverHom` and
    34	  `compactSpace_carveScheme` / `compactSpace_divScheme`: the **Wave-5 qc inputs**
    35	  toward `AbelSourceData.isProper` (`AbelianVariety/AbelSource.lean`).
    36	* `locallyOfFiniteType_carveSchemeOverHom` / `locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom`:
    37	  the **DAT-glue lft certificate** for the 01JJ chart family.
    38	* `isSeparated_carveSchemeOverHom` / `isSeparated_divSchemeOverHom` and
    39	  `isSeparated_carveScheme` / `isSeparated_divScheme`: separatedness over `k` and
    40	  absolute — with lft and qc, the `IsProper` constituents short of universal closedness.
    41	* `DivQProjBundle` / `divQProj`: the §4.1 bundle verbatim, the single citable
    42	  certificate for **DAT-G**'s quasi-projective charts.
    43	
    44	## Honest boundary (§4.1, BINDING)
    45	
    46	PROJECTIVITY of the Grassmannian (Plücker) is **not** delivered — nothing here is an
    47	ample bundle or a valuative/universal-closedness certificate.  "Quasi-projective" is
    48	consumed as the bundle above; if a consumer needs honest projectivity (or universal
    49	closedness of `grPair`, e.g. for the properness of `Div^g` feeding
    50	`AbelSourceData.isProper`), that is a NEW brick negotiated by that consumer's
    51	worksheet, not silently absorbed here.
    52	-/

# Global immersion of the Plucker morphism

The inverse image of the standard projective open indexed by `I` is exactly
the range of the `I`-th affine Grassmannian chart. On this open, the global
Plucker morphism is therefore identified with the local immersion proved in
`GrassmannianPluckerImmersion`. Since the standard projective opens cover the
target, the global Plucker morphism is an immersion.

noncomputable section

namespace AlgebraicGeometry
namespace Grassmannian

/-- The range of a Grassmannian chart localization is the principal open cut
out by its transition minor. -/
theorem chartIncl_opensRange (d r : ℕ) (I J : PluckerIndex d r) :
    (chartIncl d r I.1 J.1 I.2 J.2).opensRange =
      PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (minorDet d r I.1 J.1 I.2 J.2) := by
  change (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d × {q : Fin r // q ∉ I.1}) ℤ)
      (Localization.Away (minorDet d r I.1 J.1 I.2 J.2))))).opensRange = _
  exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext
    (PrimeSpectrum.localization_away_comap_range
      (Localization.Away (minorDet d r I.1 J.1 I.2 J.2))
      (minorDet d r I.1 J.1 I.2 J.2))

/-- Inside one affine Grassmannian chart, the inverse image of another chart's
range is the overlap localization. -/

/-!
# Projective and H-quasi-projective morphisms

This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that
Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide. A morphism is projective when it factors as
a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.

A morphism is **H-quasi-projective** when it factors through a quasi-compact
immersion into such a projective space, following the finite-projective-space
convention of [Stacks, Tag 01VV].  The quasi-compactness is part of the
definition: without it the predicate only records an immersion/relative very
ampleness and need not imply finite type.  This predicate is not asserted to
be equivalent over arbitrary bases to every formulation using relative ample
line bundles.  Both predicates are stable under base change.

The line-bundle-carrying refinement used by the Quot construction remains in
`Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean`; that refinement is universe-monomorphic because
its Serre twist is built by the project-local sheaf gluing engine.
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)

For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The degree at a field point -/

/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))

section DegAt

variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
@[simp]
theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]

/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]

/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
  rfl

/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
  rw [← picEtMap_comp]

/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'

end DegAt

/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
    degAt lam t = 0}
  one_mem' := by
    intro K _ _ t
    exact degAt_one t
  mul_mem' := by
    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
  inv_mem' := by
    intro a ha K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]

/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
          degAt lam t = 0 :=
  Iff.rfl

variable (C) in
/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
points. -/
def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))

/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
@[simp]
theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
  rfl

variable (C) in
/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
functor. -/
def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
  map_id T := by
    ext lam U
    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
  map_comp g h := by
    ext lam U
    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))

@[simp]
theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
  rfl

variable (C) in
/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
  naturality _ _ _ := rfl

end

events.text: The Kleiman comparison has exposed two precise gaps: the existing “quasi-projective bundle” only records an embedding package, and the current coequalizer lives after étale sheafification rather than in schemes. I’m finishing the independent audits now, then I’ll take the strongest self-contained geometric unit that closes one of those gaps without overstating the endpoint.
